Commentary.Commentary: We are back for South Africa's reply! Pakistan are making their way out to the middle and spread out to take their respective field positions. Aiden Markram and Tony de Zorzi are the two openers for South Africa. Khurram Shahzad has the new ball in his hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Right then, Pakistan have posted a somewhat decent total and with the ball still moving around, their pacers will come into this game. South Africa needs to get a good start and try to get through some testing conditions out there. Their main aim should be to be proactive, as that is the best way to play on this wicket. Join us in a bit for the hosts' batting.

Pakistan would be a bit disappointed as at one stage, they were looking set for getting something near 300. The openers took their time but formed a solid base. However, a crazy hour in the first session saw them lose four wickets in a flash. Then came the 81-run stand between Mohammad Rizwan and Kamran Ghulam with the latter scoring a fifty as well that got them back on track. After their dismissal, Salman Agha and Aamer Jamal added some crucial runs before the last pair showed some good fight to push the total over the 200-run mark.

Pakistan managed to add just 2 runs after Tea! Dane Paterson was the real star of the show for South Africa with his fantastic five-wicket haul. The debutant, Corbin Bosch just missed out on one ending with four scalps but played a crucial role here. Kagiso Rabada bowled unbelievably well but had nothing to show for as the Proteas also dropped a few catches in the middle otherwise, they could have restricted the visitors much earlier. Marco Jansen was a bit expensive but cleaned up the innings.

OUT! CAUGHT! It only took three deliveries after the break to wrap up Pakistan's innings. This one is bowled full and just outside off, nips in, takes off after pitching. Khurram Shahzad opens up his body to pull it towards the leg side but it takes the leading edge and stands up tall in the sky. Dane Paterson stationed at mid-wicket stedies himself under the ball and completes the catch easily in the end. Pakistan are bundled out for a mere 211 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the last session! The sun is out now and the players are already in their positions. Khurram Shahzad and Mohammad Abbas will want to score as many as possible for Pakistan. Marco Jansen to bowl the first over of this session. Let's go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

The ball is still swinging after 57 overs which adds to the bowlers' advantage. Pakistan will come out to add more runs as their last partnership will do whatever they can. South Africa will want to wrap things up as soon as possible and look forward to their batting. Join us at 1.30 pm GMT for what promises to be an exciting final session!

The tailenders of Pakistan came out to bat and went as they weren’t able to handle this fiery bowling. However, the last wicket partnership has shown some grittiness by playing out the extended half an hour brilliantly and has added 20 runs till Tea. Dane Paterson was the star for South Africa, claiming three wickets in this session, taking his tally to a fifer (back-to-back fifers for him in the last two test matches) in this first inning. Corbin Bosch also chipped in two wickets in this session to make it an overall four. They both bowled with great rhythm and the latter will aim for an individual fifer after Tea.

Mohammad Rizwan contributed 27 runs before falling into the slip cordon. Two quick wickets at 142/6 put Pakistan under pressure but all-rounders Salman Agha and Aamer Jamal steadied the innings with a promising partnership of 47 runs where the latter survived two drop catches in the slip and then chopped on after making 26. Salman Agha departed just ahead of the scheduled Tea which made it worse for Pakistan as they have slipped out from 189/6 to 189/9 in a matter of time.

SESSION SUMMARY - 33 overs, 121 runs, 5 wickets! At Tea, South Africa holds the upper hand in a contested session. However, they would have been frustrated not being able to take the last wicket in the extended 30 minutes. Pakistan are struggling at 209/9, having started the session at 88/4 after 24 overs. Kamran Ghulam and Mohammad Rizwan added a crucial 81-run partnership, with Kamran scoring his maiden fifty of the series. He played aggressively but was dismissed trying to hit a lofted shot.
Pitched up and around off, Mohammad Abbas opens the face of his bat and guides it through point for a brace. TEA ON DAY 1 HAS BEEN CALLED NOW!

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! South Africa finally got rid of Kamran Ghulam who was starting to look really dangerous here. He got under the skins of the Proteas with a few words and scored a fine half-century before being dismissed. Pakistan have to build another partnership if they want to get something around 300 and a lot will depend on the experienced Mohammad Rizwan. OUT! TAKEN! Not safe this time! An outrageous shot and Kamran Ghulam has thrown away his wicket here. Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session! The players are already out in the middle now. Mohammad Rizwan and Kamran Ghulam will resume batting for Pakistan. Kagiso Rabada to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Pakistan will be a bit disappointed that, despite managing to see off the first hour without any casualties, they let that position slip. If Rizwan and Ghulam continue to bat in the same counter-attacking fashion, South Africa won't mind it, as it opens avenues for them to strike. It promises to be another entertaining session. Do join us back at 10.40 am GMT for the start of the second session. Cheers!

After the first hour, which saw the tourists reach 36/0, fortunes quickly turned in favour of the hosts. Debutant Corbin Bosch struck with his first delivery in Test cricket, triggering what turned out to be a frenetic hour of play. Dane Paterson soon got into the act, and the visiting side slipped from 36/0 to 56/4, losing 4 wickets for just 20 runs due to a combination of disciplined bowling and indifferent batting. Despite the collapse, Mohammad Rizwan and Kamran Ghulam did not shy away from taking their chances and attempted to rebuild the innings with some counterattacking strokes.

Well, that's the end of an entertaining session to kickstart the Boxing Day Test. It turned out to be a tale of two halves, with South Africa dominating the second half of the session to head into the break as the happier of the two sides. Having been sent in to bat, the first hour was always going to be a stern test for Pakistan. Saim Ayub and Shan Masood navigated it unscathed despite a probing opening spell from Kagiso Rabada. There were multiple plays and misses, and on the rare occasions when the ball caught the edge, it failed to carry, hinting at the slower nature of the pitch.

Commentary.Commentary: All set for the action to commence in this series opener! It’s a cloudy morning with a mix of blue and grey skies in Centurion, but thankfully, it remains dry as the umpires make their way out to the middle. Temba Bavuma and Co. are in a huddle before taking their respective positions in the field. With no Abdullah Shafique in the XI, Pakistan will field a new opening pair, with captain Shan Masood set to partner Saim Ayub at the top. Kagiso Rabada has the new ball in hand. Three slips, a gully and a short leg in place. Here we go!
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Shan Masood (C), Saim Ayub, Babar Azam, Kamran Ghulam, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Saud Shakeel, Salman Agha, Aamer Jamal, Naseem Shah, Khurram Shahzad, Mohammad Abbas.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Aiden Markram, Tony de Zorzi, Ryan Rickelton, Tristan Stubbs, Temba Bavuma (C), David Bedingham, Kyle Verreynne (WK), Corbin Bosch (On debut), Marco Jansen, Kagiso Rabada, Dane Paterson.
TOSS - South Africa have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

Traditionally, Centurion's pitch has provided pace and bounce, making it an exciting venue for fast bowlers. With overcast conditions expected on all five days, the seamers are likely to remain a constant threat, making this a potentially challenging surface for the batters. With both teams eager to seize the early advantage, this promises to be a thrilling contest of skill, strategy, and determination. The first day will set the tone for the rest of the series, and the stage is perfectly set for a battle of nerves and talent. Stay tuned for the toss.

On the other hand, Pakistan enter this series with renewed confidence after a dominant 3-0 sweep in the ODI series against South Africa. Their ODI triumph will be fresh in the minds of their players, and they will look to translate that success into the longer format. The return of Mohammad Abbas after 3 years to their pace battery adds a new dimension to their attack, and it will be interesting to see how Pakistan plan to counter South Africa's batting strength. On the batting front, the onus will be on their seasoned players like Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan and the captain Shan Masood to lead the charge.

With their eyes firmly set on securing a place in the World Test Championship final at Lord's in 2025, South Africa know that winning here is paramount. They are just a win away from cementing their spot in the WTC final, so the pressure is on them to deliver. The Proteas have been in solid form and will be looking to continue their strong Test record, especially against Pakistan, who have not won a single Test match in this part of the world in 17 years. The ever-reliable Tristan Stubbs, Aiden Markram, and Temba Bavuma will be key figures in the batting department for the hosts. The bowling attack, led by Kagiso Rabada, supported by Marco Jansen, and the debutant, Corbin Bosch will be eager to exploit any opportunity that comes their way.

Hello and welcome to Day 1 of the first Test match between South Africa and Pakistan from the iconic SuperSport Park in Centurion. We are in for an exciting two-match series as two intriguing teams in world cricket battle it out and it all kicks off here on Boxing Day.
